title: Synthesize incident briefs and auto-create postmortems with PD/Slack attachments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: Currently on-call responders must manually gather traces, metrics, and recent deployment context to produce a postmortem. This delays follow-up, reduces consistency across incidents, and makes it harder to tie regressions to model/runtime rollouts. Goal: build an automated incident brief generator that listens to PagerDuty incidents and Slack incident channels, synthesizes a compact triage brief from tracing hooks, metric anomalies, and recent deploy metadata, and auto-creates a postmortem draft in Confluence (or the configured docs system) with attachments and links back to the originating PD incident and Slack channel.
acceptance_criteria: When a PagerDuty incident is acknowledged with tag 'auto-brief', the system creates a Confluence postmortem draft with title format 'PM: <service> - <short incident summary> - <YYYY-MM-DD>'
The brief includes the top 3 slowest traces (by p95 latency uplift) with links to the trace viewer, a thumbnail flamegraph URL, and a computed anomaly score for each trace
Include a metrics snapshot (error rate, request rate, 50/95/99 latencies) for the 15 minutes before and after the incident start
A Slack message is posted to the incident channel summarizing the brief and including the Confluence draft link and a single-click 'start postmortem' button (opens draft in edit mode)
Postmortem draft contains pre-filled sections: summary, timeline, impact, root cause hypothesis, mitigations, follow-ups, and owners; persistent checklist items are created for required fields
System is idempotent: re-sending the same PD event does not create duplicate drafts; drafts are updated if the incident is enriched later
Operations team can opt-out per-service via config; default on for 'redwood-serving' and 'console' services
Rate limits respected: do not create more than 2 auto-drafts per service per hour to avoid noise
implementation_notes: Event source: subscribe to PagerDuty webhooks (incident.trigger, incident.acknowledge, incident.resolve) and an optional Slack incident-channel webhook for context enrichment
Trace extraction: query tracing API for spans tagged with the incident trace_id or within the incident time window; rank by delta in p95 compared to 7-day baseline
Anomaly scoring: combine z-score for error rate and latency uplift, normalized to 0-100; threshold 35 for 'significant'
Postmortem creation: use Confluence API with templating; store mapping PD incident -> confluence_id in the incidents DB for idempotency
Security note: ensure no sensitive payloads (PII, secrets) are included in drafts; scrub user emails and token values before pushing content
Fallback: if Confluence unavailable, create a GitHub issue in 'redwood-postmortems' repo as a secondary draft
Instrumentation: add a 'brief_generation' metric with labels service,result (success/failure), latency_ms, and a counter for suppressed/duplicated attempts
Permissions: Confluence bot account should be scoped to create pages only in the 'Operations' space; PD integration uses a read-only API key for incident metadata
test_plan: Unit tests for anomaly scoring logic with synthetic time-series inputs
Integration tests: simulate PagerDuty webhook flow and assert Confluence page creation, Slack notification, and idempotency on duplicate events
Load test: fire 200 PD events in 1 minute against the staging generator to confirm rate limiting and backpressure behaviour
Security test: static analysis for templates to ensure no template injection; manual review of sample drafts for PII leakage
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable for service tag 'redwood-internal' and internal oncall only for 2 weeks
Phase 2: expand to 'redwood-serving' and 'console' with feature-flagged rollout by account
Phase 3: make opt-in default for customer-facing services and add admin console toggle per-service
Rollback: toggle feature off and delete any auto-created drafts from last 24h via cleanup job if false positives rise above threshold
comments: 2025-11-10 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created. Motivation from repeated delays in postmortem starts and inconsistent RCA formats. Suggested minimal viable brief with traces + metrics + deploy context.

2025-11-12 - Marco Li: Spiked trace extraction from tracing-api; found that p95 comparisons are expensive for long windows. Proposal: precompute 7-day baselines once per hour and cache in Redis to speed ranking.
2025-11-14 - Emily Chen (SRE): Raised concern about PD event volume causing draft spam. Added requirement for per-service rate limit and a suppression toggle for mass-alert incidents.
2025-11-16 - Marco Li: Implemented basic Confluence template integration and a stub Slack notification. PR opened: GH#2387. Needs security review for bot credentials.
2025-11-19 - Security (J. Morales): Confirmed Confluence bot scopes are acceptable; requested additional scrubbing for headers and query params before storing examples in drafts.
2025-11-20 - Marco Li: Integration tests passing on staging for single incident flow. Next: add anomaly scoring unit tests and run load test. Blocking: finalize rate limit config UX with PM.
